Theme

Latin word

spēs

spēs, speī f.

noun, fifth declension · Declension on Wiktionary

hope; promise, hope (of a young person); hope, prospect

In this lexicon

  • hope

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Att. 9.10.3: ut aegrōtō, dum anima est, spēs esse dīcitur; Traupman 154; Traupman 329

  • potential

    the recommended word · classical · Matius in Cic. Fam. 11.28.6: optimae speī adulēscentī; Cic. Cael. 80: adulēscentiam plēnam speī maximae

  • prospect

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Fam. 14.4.3: sī est spēs nostrī reditūs

Notes

  1. 1speī: short e in the genitive (Lewis & Short spēi). De Vaan 580 heads the entry spēs, speī. After a consonant the e of the fifth-declension genitive is short: Lewis & Short itself prints fidĕi, and gives rēi only for Lucretius (s.v. rēs).

Examples

  • sī est spēs nostrī reditūs, eam cōnfīrmēs et rem adjuvēs

    if there is any prospect of my return, strengthen it and help the matter alongCic. Fam. 14.4.3

    In the entry for prospect

  • cum in spem magis futūrae multitūdinis quam ad id quod tum hominum erat mūnīrent

    for they built their walls for the prospect of a future population rather than for the people they had thenLiv. 1.8.4

    In the entry for prospect
